body: I think we can just blank out the line in the source before parsing. I can't think of a reason that this would break anything.

I don't think it would break anything if it is blanked out. If it were its
own type, it might support future rules or plugins which enforce shebang
paths. That could easily be worked around though. Calling `getSourceLines`
would fill the need.
On Oct 7, 2014 7:20 PM, "Nicholas C. Zakas" notifications@github.com
wrote:

> I think we can just blank out the line in the source before parsing. I
> can't think of a reason that this would break anything.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/1352#issuecomment-58296559.

I think this could probably break the `no-multiple-empty-lines` rule.

Given the following example code:

``` js
#!/usr/bin/env node

var foo = 'bar';
```

After we blank the shebang line out, this would be:

``` js



var foo = 'bar';
```

If you have `no-multiple-empty-lines` enabled with the default configuration, this would raise a warning.

Ugh, what a mess. Transforming into a comment is what gave us a problem in the first place.

Okay, reload, maybe the answer is to leave the text, let Esprima transform it into a comment, and then remove the comment from the AST?
This could work. But we should also remove it from `trailingComments`/`leadingComments` which might be added to several nodes.
I think it would only be added as a leading comment on the first node in the body.
I’ve tried out a few patters with the esprima online parser, seems you are right.
Looks like Esprima doesn't actually do this automatically, only esvalidate does. So basically this change is to remove the comment node from what we're already doing.

issue.body: The  `spaced-line-comment` rule still has a workaround for shebang comments. This is not longer necessary since shebang comments are removed from the AST in #1352.

body:
This issue breaks my code:
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
':'; // # comment; exec /usr/bin/env node "$0" "$@"
```
If there is a newline after shebang, bash don't start the node, and all script considered to be a shell script instead of JS.

Such sort of code is met in global utilities (which are installed by npm i -g).

http://sambal.org/2014/02/passing-options-node-shebang-line/

@Dzenly Please open a new issue and provide repro steps. All ESLint does here is convert the shebang into a comment *for parsing*; it should not edit the contents of your file in general, unless a rule is doing some sort of autofix on that line (which is pretty unlikely).
I am about --fix option. My webstorm is setup for eslint --fix on file save and now I can not use webstorm for this file. Ok, I will think about advice to open a new issue.

@Dzenly What you are describing is likely not related to this issue. Please open a new issue and please fill out [this template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eslint/eslint/master/templates/bug-report.md) (hopefully will be pre-rendered into the new issue form). There are a lot of pieces of information that we need, which you aren't providing here. Again, this should be further discussed in a new issue, not this issue. Thanks!
